sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that all mitzvos contain both aspects of chukim (statutes) and mishpatim (ordinances), and that Moshe's knowledge of the reason for the Parah Adumah allowed him to fulfill it with reason, yet the unique aspect of this mitzvah is that its statute (supernal will) is revealed.

translations.translation: And this is that in all the mitzvos there are these two matters of chukim and mishpatim,
that from the aspect of the ratzon (will) of the mitzvos — all the mitzvos are chukim,
and their fulfillment must be in the manner of kabbalas ol (acceptance of the yoke),
"A chok I have decreed, a decree I have issued."
And from the aspect of the matter of the taamei hamitzvos (reasons for the mitzvos) — all the mitzvos are mishpatim,
and their fulfillment must be
(also)
from the aspect of the reason.
And because Moshe knew the reason of the mitzvah of Parah (the Red Heifer),
he also fulfilled this mitzvah from the aspect of the reason
[unlike every other person,
the fulfillment of the mitzvah of Parah Adumah from the aspect of the reason is
that he contemplates that even this mitzvah has a reason].
And based on this, it will be understood simply that even by Moshe there was not, G-d forbid, a lack of fulfillment of mitzvos in the manner of "A chok I have decreed, a decree I have issued,"
for this matter in the fulfillment of mitzvos is from the aspect of the ratzon of the mitzvos.
But this explanation requires additional explanation,
for the superiority of the mitzvah of Parah Adumah over all the mitzvos is,
that in all the mitzvos,
the reason within them conceals the ratzon,
and in the mitzvah of Parah Adumah, which has no reason
(in human intellect)
the ratzon is revealed
[and the explanation of "This is the chok of the Torah" is that all the mitzvos of the Torah are a chok like Parah Adumah].
And from that which it is said "They shall take to you,"
that the heifer is called by the name of Moshe,
it implies,
that the unique matter in the mitzvah of Parah Adumah,
that the chok within it
(ratzon above reason)
is revealed,
is also regarding Moshe,
and seemingly,
since Moshe knew the reason of Parah,
what is the difference for Moshe between the mitzvah of Parah Adumah and all the mitzvos.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the connection of Psalm 90, "A prayer of Moshe," to the redemptions of 19 Kislev and 12-13 Tammuz, explaining that it is the prayer of a wealthy person.

translations.translation: D)
And this will be understood by prefacing what is said
"A prayer of Moshe."
And it is brought in the Zohar
that "A prayer of Moshe" is the prayer of a wealthy person.
And to note from what was said by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Baal HaGeulah (Master of the Redemption), in his well-known sichah,
that the chapter "A prayer of Moshe" is connected to the redemption of 19 Kislev
[as is known that the Alter Rebbe would say each day the daily portion of Tehillim as divided for the days of the month,
and since the chapter "A prayer of Moshe" is the beginning of the monthly Tehillim portion for the 19th day of the month,
behold, he said on his day of redemption
(19 Kislev)
this chapter],
from this it is understood,
that this chapter is also connected to the redemption of 12 and 13 Tammuz,
the redemption of the Nasi of our generation, the successor of the Baal HaGeulah of 19 Kislev.
[And particularly in this year,
that on 12 Tammuz,
the birthday of the Baal HaGeulah,
is the beginning of the year of the tzaddik of the Baal HaGeulah,
and on it they begin to say the chapter of "tzaddik" which in Tehillim is the chapter "A prayer of Moshe"].
And behold, its matter and content of this chapter is "A prayer of Moshe"
[for the matters that follow in the chapter
(after the words "A prayer of Moshe, the man of G-d")
are the matters that Moshe said in his prayer
(particular matters),
but its general matter of the chapter
[which is also the name of the chapter]
is "A prayer of Moshe"],
that "A prayer of Moshe" is the prayer of a wealthy person
(as above).
And from this it is understood,
that the connection of the chapter to the redemption of 19 Kislev and 12 Tammuz is primarily from the aspect of its matter of the chapter as a whole — "A prayer of Moshe,"
the prayer of a wealthy person,
as will be explained in section 13.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies the Rebbe Rashab's question on the concept of a wealthy person's prayer, explaining that Moshe's spiritual wealth meant he lacked nothing, making the nature of his prayer a profound question.

translations.translation: E)
And this will be understood by prefacing the precise point of the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory in his maamar beginning "A prayer of Moshe,"
behold, the matter of prayer is that one prays to the Holy One, blessed be He, that He should fill his lack,
and since the wealthy person lacks nothing,
what is the matter of the prayer of a wealthy person?
And it must be said,
that this precise point is
(primarily)
regarding the prayer of Moshe.
For regarding a wealthy person in general, it can be said that his prayer is that the Holy One, blessed be He, should fill his spiritual lack.
Not so regarding Moshe, for even when he was below, his source as it is in Atzilus shone within him in a revealed manner,
to the extent that there was no partition or separation between them,
"Moshe, Moshe," the taste is not interrupted,
behold, it is understood,
that this that Moshe was wealthy in physicality is because he was wealthy in spirituality,
meaning that even in spirituality he lacked nothing,
even not a lack analogous to a horse to ride upon and a servant to run before him,
and therefore the maamar asks precisely what is the matter of the prayer of a wealthy person.
